title: Setup — Git for everyone, Node.js only for Claude Code

steps.path: The first screen after installing YouCoded, while it gets the computer ready
steps.headline: New users now wait only for Git during setup; Node.js no longer installs for everyone.
steps.changed: Node.js is gone from the setup checklist. It installs later, only when someone picks Claude Code (Log in with Claude, Install Claude Code in Settings) or opens a terminal. The line above the list now says what Git is actually for.
steps.measured: 1 install instead of 2; on a clean Windows test machine Git took 8 s to download and 37 s to unpack
steps.notice: Setup is shorter. On Windows there is no admin pop-up and no dead end on PCs missing Microsoft's App Installer: Git comes from Git's own portable download into your user folder. On Linux a password window installs Git instead of a terminal command.
steps.risk: People who choose Claude Code now wait for Node.js at sign-in instead of during setup (about a minute, shown as 'Installing Claude Code…'). The Linux password window has not been tried on a real desktop yet.

steps.path: The moment the installs finish, on a Windows PC without Developer Mode
steps.headline: Once Git is in, setup goes straight to sign-in — no Developer Mode screen, no Node.js row.
steps.changed: The Windows Developer Mode step is removed (nothing in the app needs it since the old toolkit was retired), and the checklist shows only what this person actually needed.
steps.notice: Windows users skip a screen that asked them to change a system security setting through an admin prompt. Mac, Linux and people who already had Developer Mode on see no difference beyond the shorter list.
steps.risk: None known — the step's only job was the old toolkit's symbolic links, and a search of the app found nothing that still makes them.
